title: Fix DSL Kernel List-Of-Records Node Count Overflow
description:
framework/kernel/dsl/schema/rs (used via store::DocumentDsl::parse_dsl) fails to parse a workflow.nodes table row whose inputs/outputs columns are each a bracketed list of records with multiple key=value fields on one line, e.g.:
    node-app-draw-1 app-draw-1 40 80 160 72 [ id="app-draw-1:out:in" resource-kind="2d.drawing" direction=in ] [ id="app-draw-1:out:out" resource-kind="2d.drawing" direction=out ]
Parsing throws TextError { message: "node count exceeds max_nodes limit (1000001 > 1000000)", span pointing at the second field ("resource-kind") inside the first bracketed list item }. Something in the list-of-records / table parser (check_nodes call sites in framework/kernel/dsl/schema/rs/lib.rs, around lines 380/400/737/779) mishandles a record with more than one inline field inside a [...] list, causing a runaway loop that keeps appending to a node-count accumulator until it trips the 1,000,000 safety limit. Deterministic, single-threaded, 100% reproducible — not a race.

Repro: <semio_framework_os::OsProjection as store::DocumentDsl>::parse_dsl(text) where text is s/plugin/space/example/demo.s (line 5 above). Confirmed NOT caused by the constitutional-crate restructuring itself — the fixture and parse call are byte-identical to the pre-split monolith, now relocated to s/plugin/space/shared/rs/lib.rs's parse_demo_space_document(). framework/product/os/core/rs's own tests only round-trip a print_dsl-generated OsProjection sample with at most 1 port per node, so this hand-authored multi-field-per-line list syntax was never exercised before.

Impact: blocks every test in the newly-split semio-s-app-space-home-ui, semio-s-app-space-space-dsl, semio-s-app-space-space-engine, semio-s-app-space-space-pack, and semio-s-app-space-space-ui crates that touches space_shared::demo_space_projection()/parse_demo_space_document() — first failure panics inside a LazyLock, poisoning it and cascading failures to sibling tests in the same binary.

Task: investigate the list-of-records parsing path in framework/kernel/dsl/schema/rs and fix the underlying accumulation bug so multi-field bracketed list records parse correctly. Discovered while working the parent ticket.
summary:
Root-caused and fixed the reported "node count exceeds max_nodes limit (1000001 > 1000000)" parse error. Two bugs stacked:

1. **Parser robustness bug (framework/kernel/dsl/schema/rs/lib.rs, `Shape::List` arm of `parse_shape`)**: a bare `Shape::Record` list element (no keyword, no brackets of its own — e.g. a list of `key=value` port records) can legitimately finish parsing having consumed zero tokens, once none of its remaining keys match the next token. `parse_record_body`'s keyed loop can't distinguish "record legitimately ended" from "unrecognized key" — both just `break`. The `Shape::List` loop had no protection against this: it kept calling `parse_shape` on a stuck cursor, pushing an empty record every iteration, until `check_nodes`'s 1,000,000 safety limit tripped — far from the actual offending token, with a useless error message. Fixed by comparing cursor position before/after each list-element parse and returning an immediate, correctly-spanned `TextError` ("list element made no progress ... — likely an unrecognized field key") the instant an iteration makes no progress. `parse_table_list` and `Shape::Statements` were checked and are not vulnerable (both always consume ≥1 token per iteration structurally).

2. **Data bug (the actual trigger)**: `s/plugin/space/example/demo.s` used DSL key `resource-kind=` in its `workflow.nodes` table's `inputs`/`outputs` port lists, but the real field is `OsMediaPort::artifact_kind` (framework/product/os/core/rs/lib.rs:2977-2981), which the `dsl::DslRecord` derive's `to_kebab` naming law renders as `artifact-kind`. Renamed all 10 occurrences in demo.s to `artifact-kind`. Also found and fixed the same `program-id` vs `plugin-id` mismatch in demo.s's `app-instances` table header (real field: `OsAppInstance::plugin_id`).

3. **Same root-cause bug found in 5 JSON test fixtures**: framework/product/os/core/fixtures/{no-dirty,dead-end,chain,single-edge,diamond}.json all used `"resourceKind"` instead of `"artifactKind"` — same `OsMediaPort` field, different serialization (serde camelCase JSON vs DSL kebab). This was causing `workflow_fixtures_match_expected_deliveries` in semio-framework-os to panic on whichever fixture the (unordered) `read_dir` iteration hit first. Fixed all 5.

Verified: semio-framework-kernel-dsl-schema (27/27 pass, no regressions from the new guard), semio-framework-os (53/54 pass — 1 remaining failure, `create_ephemeral_os_space_has_no_backbone`, is unrelated to this bug — an ID-prefix assertion, confirmed untouched by these changes — flagged as a separate follow-up task, not fixed here), and all 5 originally-blocked crates (semio-s-app-space-home-ui 8/8, semio-s-app-space-space-dsl 2/2, semio-s-app-space-space-engine 2/2, semio-s-app-space-space-pack 2/2, semio-s-app-space-space-ui 37/37) now pass in full.
